Are you a researcher or developer at CERTH thinking of diving into the open-source world, or do you have
inquiries regarding your open-source software or hardware designs?

This documentation covers the essential topics you need to know before and after open-sourcing a project
at CERTH: copyright, licensing, due diligence, and best practices for a successful and sustainable
open-source release.

## What you will find here

- **Key Concepts** — foundational knowledge on copyright, licensing, due diligence, and what the
  open-sourcing process looks like at CERTH.
- **Recommendations** — concrete, actionable guidance on how to apply copyright notices, choose a
  licence, and structure your project for publication.
- **Project** — space for ongoing and future CERTH OSPO initiatives.

## Getting started

If you are releasing a project for the first time, a recommended reading order is:

1. [Copyright](key-concepts/copyright.qmd) — understand who owns what
2. [Licensing](key-concepts/licensing.qmd) — choose the right terms for sharing
3. [Due Diligence](key-concepts/due-diligence.qmd) — check what needs to be verified before going public
4. [What to Expect](key-concepts/what-to-expect.qmd) — a walkthrough of the release process at CERTH

For detailed implementation guidance, see the [Recommendations](recommendations/copyright.qmd) section.

## Contact

Have questions not covered here? Reach out to the CERTH OSPO team at **ospo@certh.gr**.
